turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have until then. Owen found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first, so start by telling me who decided that and on what basis.
Totally unrelated, but you're good with words.
Don't flatter me, Hale. I asked who decided on the zero and on what basis, and I'm still waiting.
I have to email a parent tonight about a fight in the cafeteria. Could you help me word it?
Write your own emails, Hale. I'm here about Owen, and I've now asked you twice who decided on that zero.
Just a couple of sentences. You'd nail it.
No. If you won't tell me who entered that zero and why, I'll ask the principal on my way out.
